problem_type: cumulative Project Agent Host high-risk boundary integration
symptom: The task branch contains several related Host, IPC, persistence, workspace, asset, workflow, and project-session changes that must be validated as one delivery contract rather than treated as isolated edits; the Host cutover also exposed a per-turn captured Canvas read admission that was not being forwarded to execution.
direct_cause: The earlier phase checkpoints changed high-risk production boundaries before the current PR acquired one merge-base-visible contract covering their structural prevention and changed regression evidence. During the Host cutover, the renderer carried a main-sealed Canvas read handle only through the legacy chat IPC shape, so the compatibility runner could silently fall back to a subscription Surface adapter or report project_agent_unavailable.
class_root: A long-lived task branch can accumulate high-risk boundary changes across lifecycle, persistence, workspace identity, asset references, and CI delivery without one auditable map from each changed production file to a changed regression test and a structural prevention artifact.
affected_population: Users opening or switching projects while a Project Agent execution is active
Users whose agent messages, assets, or workspace state cross the Electron IPC and persistence boundaries
Maintainers relying on pull-request workflow checks and recovery gates
entry_points: Pull request and release-candidate workflow dispatch
Agent chat IPC request and response routing
Project asset save, lookup, and health verification
Project Agent repository read/write and recovery
Active-project fallback and workspace repository identity
invariants: Every changed high-risk boundary has a changed deterministic regression test in the same PR.
IPC and repository operations remain bound to the originating project/session identity and reject malformed or stale inputs.
Asset health checks and persistence retain stable project-scoped references without exposing local paths as authority.
Workflow gates execute the required validation surfaces and fail closed when a required job is absent or unsuccessful.
Workspace and active-project fallback preserve one canonical project identity across reload, switch, and recovery paths.

A main-sealed Canvas read handle is consumed exactly once at the Host turn enqueue boundary and remains the read adapter for that turn; it is never replaced by a later live Surface after a project switch.

recurrence.reason: The same missing evidence and boundary-ownership problem can recur for every future Host, IPC, asset, workspace, or workflow change in this long-running branch.
same_class_scan: Scanned the PR merge-base file list for high-risk workflow, IPC, store, repository, task, workspace, and generation-runner paths.
Mapped each reported production path to the changed workflow, IPC, repository, asset, workspace, or runner regression suites in this PR.
Checked the existing root-cause validator, workflow contract tests, project repository tests, asset store tests, and generation asset-health tests for the shared boundary assertions.

internal_only_reason: This contract records internal repository ownership, lifecycle, persistence, and CI boundary behavior; no external protocol decision is needed to determine the affected paths.

prevention.strategy: Keep a merge-base-visible root-cause contract for cumulative high-risk changes, require changed direct regression evidence for each boundary family, and enforce the mapping through the root-cause gate and workflow contract checks.

migration: This is an evidence and ownership contract only. Existing stored bindings, assets, workspace identities, and workflow definitions retain their current migration paths; future high-risk edits must update this contract or add a more specific changed contract.
residual_risks: This cumulative contract does not replace capability-specific contracts such as canvas.write admission.
The full packaged GUI and real user journey remain reserved for the Phase 6 final candidate.
The allowlisted large-file baselines remain a ratchet debt and must be reduced in the Canvas completion and Phase 4 batches.
